title: I built an AI-assisted used car dealership game. Here's what I've learned.
author: vepacls
selftext:
I've been building Dealer King, a browser-based used car dealership simulator, with the help of ChatGPT and Replit's AI development tools.

I work in the automotive sales industry, and I wanted to turn real dealership decisions into a game: buying cars at auction, dealing with hidden faults, managing repair costs, negotiating with buyers and reinvesting profits.

My approach has been to use my automotive experience to design the gameplay, work with AI tools to implement features, and then test and refine everything through multiple iterations. AI has been used extensively in development, including coding and some visual and promotional materials. The game itself doesn't require players to use generative AI.

One example is the onboarding experience. I used AI-assisted development to implement the first-car purchase and first-sale flow, then tested and refined it to make the early decisions easier to understand without removing the risk of buying a bad car.

One thing I've learned is that getting a feature working is often easier than making the gameplay feel balanced and rewarding. A car that looks like a bargain can turn into a terrible deal once the repair costs start adding up.

Dealer King is currently free to play in your browser:

[https://playdealerking.com](https://playdealerking.com)

For those of you building games with AI-assisted tools: what's been your biggest challenge — implementing features or making the actual gameplay fun?

comments.author: Grokhnars
comments.body: the biggest challenge is to stop myself... step back .. overview the code and then carry on working
